A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RExBench study. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained tasks, experiments, and analyses across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of nine agent configurations, including task performance, hint experiments, resource consumption, and error analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of twelve main agent configurations and two additional Claude 4.5 Opus configurations, alongside quantitative and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The benchmark workflow and retained aider/OpenHands procedures remain unchanged: agents edit existing research code, submit patches, and undergo controlled execution against private gold outcomes. Appendix A proposes future improvements such as scratchpads and repair mechanisms without implementing them.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same twelve research-extension tasks and three hint conditions. v3 Table 1 adds descriptions of existing extensions; the retained WinoDict instructions and task-specific tables do not establish changed task requirements or additional domains.

E2.justification: v3 removes Claude Code and adds Claude 4 Sonnet and GPT-5 under both aider and OpenHands. Appendix I additionally evaluates Claude 4.5 Opus under both frameworks. This adds six agent–model combinations and removes one, while retaining the other eight configurations.

E3.justification: New supplementary procedures measure cyclomatic-complexity changes over gold-modified files, and manual implicit-error inspection switches from OpenHands/Claude 3.7 and Claude Code to OpenHands/Claude 4 and GPT-5. The main benchmark metrics, hint conditions, execution limit, and task hardware assignments remain stable.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands failure analysis through cases of ineffective edits, silent fallbacks, and unnecessary modifications in Appendix H, alongside a revised manual-error cohort. Appendix D adds an alternative task-complexity analysis and its relationship to edit size. Hint experiments and tool-use analysis already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Agent evaluations explicitly increase from three to five runs per task. Section 3.4 newly specifies five seeded gold runs and acceptance bounds of mean plus or minus two standard deviations, without establishing that gold-run counts changed. Existing error-bar and regression-interval practices remain; Appendix G retains a three-run description for token averages.

E6.justification: Many retained estimates change: aider/Claude 3.7 no-hint final success is 0.14 in v1 Table 4 and 0.08 in v3 Table 5, with three versus five runs. New configurations add substantial results, including OpenHands/Claude 4.5 Opus at 0.42 without hints and 0.62 with hints. Resource statistics, error distributions, and regression estimates also change.

T1.justification: The file-recall formula and task formalization are retained. Neither version develops theoretical propositions or proofs; the added complexity measurements and gold-range details concern empirical analysis and estimation.

C1.justification: The central contribution and qualitative claims remain: a contamination-resistant benchmark of research extensions, automatic execution-based evaluation, and substantial difficulty for agents operating autonomously. Updated scores and model rankings change the supporting evidence without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: v3 develops over-editing and silent failures as mechanisms, adds concrete design recommendations in Appendix A, and qualifies the benchmark's ability to distinguish similarly capable models. Its ethical discussion newly emphasizes that strong benchmark performance is insufficient evidence of reliable autonomous research coding.

D1.justification: v3 adds gold-bound calibration details, names radon and shellmetrics for complexity measurement, and supplies Hugging Face dataset and dedicated agent-repository links. It removes some virtual-machine specifications and the explicit one-line prompt previously documented in the Claude Code section, leaving OpenHands referring to the same instruction without quoting it.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands coverage of experiment planning, research coding, and software-agent evaluation, adding works such as AblationBench, AbGen, GUIDE, ResearchCodeBench, DeepCode, MLGym, and Terminal-Bench. The central distinction between novel extensions and paper replication remains; publication updates to retained references do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: v3 expands the generic task illustration into a WinoDict walkthrough, rewrites the sample instruction and substantial results/discussion passages, and reorganizes the appendices. It also separates ethical considerations from limitations and revises headings, affiliations, and citation presentation.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. Table 1 replaces source-paper titles with task summaries; comparison plots expand, metric columns are reordered, and the error table is split by framework. New complexity and Opus displays accompany relocated and reformatted existing material.

improvement.justification: Broader model comparisons, five-run evaluation, explicit gold-range documentation, and concrete failure cases improve the benchmark's characterization. These gains are tempered by incomplete integration: the abstract retains a below-44% hinted-success headline while Appendix I and Table 5 report 62%, and Appendix G retains a three-run token-summary description. The evidence supports a limited net quality improvement.
